paper_title: Tight Lower Bounds for Problems Parameterized by Rank-Width
classifications: Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
statement: We hope the tools designed in this paper could be used to design tight lower bounds 2 for more problems parameterized by rank-width. In particular, is the 2O(rw ) nO(1) time algorithm in [6] for (unweighted) Dominating Set optimal under ETH? What about the 2 2O(q·rw ) nO(1) time algorithm in [6] for q-Coloring (even when q = 3)? Finally, one could O(rw) also explore the optimality of XP algorithms parameterized by rank-width such as the n2 time algorithm in [19] for Chromatic Number. For the clique-width parameterization this was solved in [16].
context: 2 We showed the first ETH-tight lower bounds for problems with time complexity 2O(rw ) nO(1) parameterized by rank-width rw. In particular, we showed that algorithms with such time complexity are optimal for Independent Set, Weighted Dominating Set, Maximum Induced Matching, and Feedback Vertex Set. We hope the tools designed in this paper could be used to design tight lower bounds 2 for more problems parameterized by rank-width. In particular, is the 2O(rw ) nO(1) time algorithm in [6] for (unweighted) Dominating Set optimal under ETH? What about the 2 2O(q·rw ) nO(1) time algorithm in [6] for q-Coloring (even when q = 3)? Finally, one could O(rw) also explore the optimality of XP algorithms parameterized by rank-width such as the n2 time algorithm in [19] for Chromatic Number. For the clique-width parameterization this was solved in [16].
